claims.text: People keep paying for subscriptions they do not use because there is data in them, they might need the capability, and restarting is painful.
claims.quote: So it sits there, and you keep paying.

claims.text: The UK government estimates that 8% of active subscriptions are unwanted, about 9.7 million contracts.
claims.quote: estimates that 8% of active subscriptions are unwanted, about 9.7 million contracts

value.unit: percent of active UK subscriptions unwanted

claims.text: On 9 August 2026 the government put the total at around 155 million active subscriptions, with consumers spending about 1.6 billion pounds a year on ones they do not want.
claims.quote: with consumers spending an estimated £1.6 billion a year on ones they don't actually want

value.unit: pounds a year on unwanted subscriptions

claims.text: Citizens Advice found in 2024 that people had spent 688 million pounds in the previous year on subscriptions they did not use.
claims.quote: people had spent £688 million in the previous year on subscriptions they did not use

value.unit: pounds in a year on unused subscriptions

claims.text: A subscription is a discount for committing to regular use, not rent on something you have the right to ignore.
claims.quote: A subscription is a discount for committing to regular use. It is not rent on something you have the right to ignore.

claims.text: Step one is a polite email asking the company for a detailed analysis of how much the account was used, with our own analysis from statements and dashboards run in parallel.
claims.quote: can you give me a detailed analysis of how much this account has been used?

claims.text: Step two, a few days later, is a friendly letter mapping what was paid and used, saying good things about the product, and asking for a suspend mode that keeps the data and a refund for unused months.
claims.quote: Then it asks for two things.

claims.text: Several large services already have a pause button: Netflix pauses a membership for a month up to three months, and Zoom lets small monthly Pro accounts pause for up to three months.
claims.quote: Several large services already have a pause button.

claims.text: Whatever the answer to the refund, stop the bleeding: export the data first, then pause or cancel.
claims.quote: The order matters: export first, then cancel.

claims.text: Adobe's US terms charge half the remaining balance for cancelling an annual plan paid monthly after the first fourteen days, which the analysis must know before the letter.
claims.quote: charge a fee of half the remaining balance for cancelling an annual plan paid monthly after the first fourteen days

claims.text: In general a company does not have to refund months paid for and not used, so most of the refunds this service asks for will be goodwill.
claims.quote: Most of the refunds this service asks for will be goodwill.

claims.text: The UK's subscription regime in the DMCC Act 2024 brings reminder notices, an easy exit and a fourteen-day cooling-off period, and on 9 August 2026 the government said it will come into force in January 2027.
claims.quote: will now come into force in January 2027

claims.text: An EU withdrawal button applies from 19 June 2026, California has required click-to-cancel since July 2025, and the FTC's rule was vacated in July 2025 and restarted in March 2026; none says refund the months I ignored.
claims.quote: All of them move the default towards the customer.

claims.text: Under UK GDPR a company must respond to an access request within one month, usually without a fee; activity logs are in scope, and a third party with authority can request on someone's behalf.
claims.quote: must respond without undue delay, and within one month of receipt of the request

claims.text: An access request is only ever a genuine request for the person's own data, never leverage, so the refund conversation stays separate.
claims.quote: An access request used as a threat is how the mechanism gets refused and how it loses its value for everybody else.

claims.text: The whole method and what is learned go into an open register under Creative Commons: contacts, templates, whether a pause exists, response times, and which companies refund and which do not.
claims.quote: we should open source the whole method, under Creative Commons, and publish what we learn as we figure it out

claims.text: The register follows the subscriptions site's rules: record, never verdict, no adjectives, silence as a row, never a first refusal, and it publishes a company's behaviour, never a person's case.
claims.quote: The register publishes a company's behaviour, never a person's case.

claims.text: A helper, a freelancer or bookkeeper working for one person, is paid 10% of the savings for the next three months and 20% of any money recovered; nothing saved, nothing paid.
claims.quote: 10% of the savings for the next three months, and 20% of any money recovered.

claims.text: For comparison, Rocket Money's bill negotiation charges 35% to 60% of the first year's savings.
claims.quote: a fee of 35% - 60% of your first year's savings

value.unit: percent of first-year savings, lower bound

claims.text: The average unwanted subscription is 14 pounds a month, so stopping one earns the helper 4.20 pounds and recovering six months earns 16.80, which only adds up if agents do the work.
claims.quote: Stopping one earns the helper 10% of three months of that, £4.20.

value.unit: pounds a month, average unwanted subscription

claims.text: Claude in Chrome drives the browser to find usage, invoices and the export button, and the freelancer interacts only when a secret is needed: a password, a two-factor code, a captcha.
claims.quote: interacts only when a secret is needed: a password, a two-factor code, a captcha

claims.text: Claude in Chrome has been available on every paid Claude plan since 26 August 2026, pauses at a login page or CAPTCHA, and is prohibited from inputting sensitive data.
claims.quote: since 26 August 2026 it is available on every paid Claude plan

claims.text: The agent writes every letter as a Gmail draft, a second reader the agent cannot skip checks it, and the freelancer sends it.
claims.quote: The freelancer reads each one and sends it.

claims.text: The vaults are the interface: documentation, tasks as folders in Issues-FS, the map of every subscription, and messages as files in Email-FS; nothing about a person leaves their vault.
claims.quote: Nothing about a person leaves their vault.

claims.text: Two controls today: secrets are entered by the freelancer, drafts are sent by the freelancer, everything else is automated, and responsibility stays with the person who sends.
claims.quote: Secrets are entered by the freelancer. Drafts are sent by the freelancer. Everything else is automated.

claims.text: Once signed in, the agent's session has the account's whole reach, and drafts only is held by an approval prompt and the freelancer, not made impossible by the tool.
claims.quote: the same login that downloads the invoices can delete the data, close the account, upgrade the plan or change the card

claims.text: Whether this work belongs in a browser-driving agent at all, or in a narrower tool, is one of the things the MVP is meant to answer.
claims.quote: Whether this kind of work belongs in a browser-driving agent at all, or in a narrower tool, is one of the things the MVP is meant to answer.

claims.text: It is a first MVP, not yet run; the statement pipeline ran in March on the owner's statements, the rest is a proposal until the beta users have tried it.
claims.quote: It is a first MVP, not yet run.

claims.text: Most refunds will be goodwill; unused months are generally not refundable as of right, and this is not legal advice.
claims.quote: the legal levers are narrower, and this is not legal advice

claims.text: The consumer rules quoted may not cover business accounts; a sole trader paying for a business tool may rest on goodwill alone.
claims.quote: The consumer rules may not cover business accounts.

claims.text: The law is as at 13 October 2026: the UK regime is not in force until January 2027, the EU button depends on transposition, the US federal rule is being written again.
claims.quote: The law is as at 13 October 2026.

claims.text: The fee split is a suggestion; contingency fees can change how a service looks to a regulator, and the card-issuer route is left out pending advice.
claims.quote: The fee split is a suggestion.

claims.text: The register has no entries yet, and a solicitor review of the publishing rule is still pending on subscriptions.sgit.ai.
claims.quote: The register has no entries yet.

claims.text: The signed-in session is the reach: the session the agent works in can do far more than the mandate, and the red rows in the figure are open controls still owed.
claims.quote: The signed-in session is the reach.

claims.text: Anthropic advises against Claude in Chrome for financial accounts and sites holding other people's personal information, so the beta runs on its users' own subscriptions first; how a person shares and revokes access is still to learn.
claims.quote: The tool's maker advises caution here.
